B's options also promise things the issue may not deliver ('Two quick fixes that take 30 seconds', 'probably set up wrong'). A's options stick more closely to the content named and avoid bait, but A's testing advice is vague and doesn't set up a real split test, which is the one area where B is clearly stronger. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): A explains the pattern more fully. Its caveats are stronger, including Apple Mail Privacy Protection, and it proposes a proper same-time split test. A's stale-'June edition' point assumes when that issue was sent, and several of its previews (B's included) invent details the issue may not contain; B has two options that are near-rewordings and only suggests comparing separate sends, which is a weak test.
